title: adoption_mode: one validated entry point for osf.toml
summary: Adds a top-level `adoption_mode` key to a repository's own `osf.toml` and funnels every reader of that file through a single parse step, `config::repo_document`, which validates the key and refuses unsupported values. The previously lenient readers — `[review] hot_paths` in changeset risk and `[scan]` in review-context redaction — now propagate read/parse errors instead of silently falling back to defaults, and the layered `load` and `--gate` path share the same parser so no reader can skip the check. A `require_adoption_mode` helper lets a command declare which modes it supports.

nodes.label: repo_document
nodes.subtitle: fn repo_document(root: &Path) -> Result<Option<toml::Value>, ConfigError>
nodes.summary: Reads and parses `<root>/osf.toml`, returning None only when the file is absent. Any other read error, invalid TOML, or unsupported adoption_mode is an error. The one entry point for non-layered readers.

nodes.label: config::load
nodes.subtitle: layered load
nodes.summary: The layered config load now parses through parse_repo_document and strips the adoption_mode key before merging, so the key never trips deny_unknown_fields but an unsupported value still fails.
